BiblicalUsage: This is wrath that bursts out, an overflow of fury, and the Bible uses it most often for God's anger against sin and for the arrogance of men. Jacob curses the fierce anger of Simeon and Levi, Isaiah says the land is darkened by the wrath of the Lord of hosts, and Ezekiel says God will pour out His indignation on a people that would not listen. It is not a slow burn; it is a flood breaking its banks.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's wrath is real and righteous, and that is good news, because a God who never burned against evil would never rescue anyone from it. His anger is the other side of His love for what is right, and it falls hardest where His patience has been refused longest.
